subject: Linear Algebra
title: Inner Product Spaces and Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization
note: Original ACADRIX practice MCQs based on the R-2025 Unit III syllabus. These are not official Anna University questions or PYQs.

questions.q: An inner product on a real vector space is a function that maps two vectors to a:
questions.explanation: For a real inner product space, the inner product of two vectors is a real number.

questions.q: The inner product of vectors u and v is commonly denoted by:
questions.explanation: Angle brackets are standard notation for an inner product.

questions.q: For the standard dot product in Rⁿ, ⟨u,v⟩ equals:
questions.explanation: The Euclidean inner product is the sum of the products of corresponding components.

questions.q: The inner product satisfies which symmetry property in a real inner product space?
questions.explanation: Real inner products are symmetric.

questions.q: Positive definiteness of an inner product requires ⟨v,v⟩ to be:
questions.explanation: An inner product is positive definite: ⟨v,v⟩>0 whenever v is nonzero.

questions.q: The norm induced by an inner product is defined by:
questions.explanation: The length or norm induced by an inner product is the square root of the self-inner-product.

questions.q: The norm of the zero vector is:
questions.explanation: Since ⟨0,0⟩=0, the induced norm of the zero vector is zero.

questions.q: Two vectors u and v are orthogonal when:
questions.explanation: Orthogonality is defined by a zero inner product.

questions.q: Two nonzero orthogonal vectors are necessarily:
questions.explanation: If one nonzero vector were a scalar multiple of another, their inner product could not be zero unless one were zero.

questions.q: The Cauchy-Schwarz inequality states that |⟨u,v⟩| is:
questions.explanation: Cauchy-Schwarz gives |⟨u,v⟩|≤||u||||v||.

questions.q: Equality in the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality occurs when the vectors are:
questions.explanation: Equality occurs precisely when one vector is a scalar multiple of the other, including the zero case.

questions.q: For nonzero vectors u and v, the angle θ between them satisfies:
questions.explanation: The inner-product definition of angle gives this normalized dot-product formula.

questions.q: If u and v are orthogonal nonzero vectors, the angle between them is:
questions.explanation: Orthogonality gives cosθ=0, so θ=90°.

questions.q: A set of vectors is called orthogonal if every pair of distinct vectors is:
questions.explanation: An orthogonal set has zero inner product between every pair of distinct vectors.

questions.q: An orthonormal set is an orthogonal set whose vectors each have:
questions.explanation: Orthonormal means mutually orthogonal and individually normalized to unit length.

questions.q: An orthogonal basis has the advantage that vector coordinates can be obtained using:
questions.explanation: For an orthogonal basis, coefficients are obtained by projecting onto the basis vectors using inner products.

questions.q: The Gram-Schmidt process converts a linearly independent set into an:
questions.explanation: Gram-Schmidt constructs an orthogonal set spanning the same subspace and can then normalize it.

questions.q: The first vector in the Gram-Schmidt process is usually chosen as:
questions.explanation: The first orthogonal vector is taken as the first vector of the given linearly independent set.

questions.q: To make a Gram-Schmidt vector into a unit vector, divide it by its:
questions.explanation: Normalization is performed by v/||v|| for a nonzero vector v.

questions.q: The projection of u onto a nonzero vector v is:
questions.explanation: The orthogonal projection formula uses the scalar ⟨u,v⟩/⟨v,v⟩.

questions.q: In Gram-Schmidt, the component of a new vector along an earlier orthogonal vector is removed by:
questions.explanation: Each previous projection is subtracted so the new vector becomes orthogonal to the earlier vectors.

questions.q: If {u₁,u₂,u₃} is an orthogonal set of nonzero vectors, then it is:
questions.explanation: Any orthogonal set of nonzero vectors is linearly independent.

questions.q: The standard basis vectors in R³ form an:
questions.explanation: The standard unit vectors are mutually orthogonal and each has norm one.

questions.q: For u=(1,2) and v=(3,4) under the standard dot product, ⟨u,v⟩ is:
For v=(3,4) in R², its Euclidean norm is:
If ⟨u,v⟩=0 and neither vector is zero, then u and v are:
questions.explanation: A zero inner product between nonzero vectors is the defining condition for orthogonality.

questions.q: For a vector v=(a,b) in R², v is a unit vector when:
questions.explanation: A unit vector has norm one, so √(a²+b²)=1.

questions.q: The Gram-Schmidt process preserves the:
questions.explanation: The resulting orthogonal vectors span the same subspace as the original linearly independent vectors.

questions.q: For an orthonormal basis {q₁,...,qₙ}, the coefficient of qᵢ in v is:
questions.explanation: With unit basis vectors, v=Σ⟨v,qᵢ⟩qᵢ.

questions.q: For any vector v and scalar c, the norm satisfies ||cv||=:
questions.explanation: Norms are absolutely homogeneous: ||cv||=|c| ||v||.
